title: Plotly traces and layout from explicit data
outcome: Construct and inspect a small Plotly figure whose trace data and layout correspond to a declared analytical view.
mechanism:
A Plotly figure contains data traces and layout instructions. A trace describes a set of marks with a type, coordinates and styling. Layout describes axes, titles, legends and other figure-level choices. Keeping these responsibilities separate makes the serialized figure inspectable rather than treating an interactive chart as an opaque object.

A scatter trace can draw markers, lines or both. Lines connect supplied coordinates according to their order; they do not infer a meaningful temporal or scientific sequence automatically. A reference line should be labeled as a model, rule or comparison rather than being visually indistinguishable from observed measurements.

In the R interface, plot_ly constructs a figure and add_trace or convenience functions add traces. Formula mappings such as ~x refer to columns in the supplied data. plotly_build resolves the object into trace and layout structures that can be checked numerically. A bar trace uses the supplied heights; it is not automatically a grouped statistical count of arbitrary raw records.

Scripts should call print(p) explicitly. The classroom captures that printed Plotly specification and renders it through its offline figure path. Bare construction of p is not a rendered result. Conversely, a correct captured specification is not proof that hover, zoom, clipping or keyboard behavior worked in a browser.

All data in these examples is inline and synthetic. The figures do not use an external tile service, remote dataset, account or live application server. The small trace grammar is useful before adding interaction because it makes the values, category identity and coordinate order independently checkable.

vocabulary.definition: A figure component describing one set of marks and its data attributes.
Figure-level settings such as axes, titles and legends.
The choice to display markers, lines or both for a scatter trace.
The serializable data and layout consumed by the chart renderer.

anatomy: Use plotly::plot_ly(data,x=~x,y=~y,type="scatter",mode="markers") for explicit points, then add_lines for a separately named rule. Apply layout for axis titles. Inspect plotly_build(p)$x$data and its layout, then print(p) to emit the widget through the classroom capture path.

worked_examples.title: Observed points and a labeled rule
worked_examples.code:
d <- data.frame(x = 1:3, observed = c(2, 4, 3), rule = c(2, 4, 6))
p <- plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~x, y = ~observed, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", name = "Observed")
p <- plotly::add_lines(p, y = ~rule, name = "Rule: 2x")
p <- plotly::layout(p, xaxis = list(title = "Input"), yaxis = list(title = "Response"), title = "Observations and an explicit comparison rule")
built <- plotly::plotly_build(p)
stopifnot(length(built$x$data) == 2)
stopifnot(max(abs(as.numeric(built$x$data[[1]]$y) - c(2, 4, 3))) < 1e-12)
stopifnot(max(abs(as.numeric(built$x$data[[2]]$y) - c(2, 4, 6))) < 1e-12)
print(p)
worked_examples.explanation: Two trace names distinguish observations from the authored rule. The checks inspect the exact y values in both traces before the object is printed.
worked_examples.expected: Two traces with observed 2/4/3 and rule2/4/6 values.

worked_examples.title: Bars represent supplied summaries
worked_examples.code:
d <- data.frame(category = c("A", "B", "C"), count = c(2, 1, 3))
p <- plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~category, y = ~count, type = "bar", name = "Observation count")
p <- plotly::layout(p, xaxis = list(type = "category", title = "Category"), yaxis = list(title = "Count", rangemode = "tozero"))
built <- plotly::plotly_build(p)$x$data[[1]]
stopifnot(identical(as.character(built$x), d$category), identical(as.numeric(built$y), d$count))
print(p)
worked_examples.explanation: The input is already a count table. Plotly draws those values; the analysis that produced the counts remains a separate responsibility.
worked_examples.expected: Three bars with named categories and supplied heights2/1/3.

exercises.prompt: Construct one marker trace from the three observed pairs.
exercises.answer: The trace contains the three source coordinates without an implied connecting trajectory.

exercises.prompt: Add and name the rule y=2x as a line trace.
exercises.hint: Keep observed and modeled quantities separate.
exercises.answer: The second trace has values 2,4,6 and a distinct explanatory name.

exercises.hint: Do not put figure-level labels into a data vector.
exercises.answer: The layout identifies the x and y quantities while trace coordinates remain unchanged.

exercises.hint: Inspect the order of x and y pairs together.
exercises.answer: A line follows supplied order; sort or group under a declared trajectory contract before connecting observations.

exercises.prompt: Build a bar figure from the supplied count table and inspect its values.
exercises.answer: Trace coordinates preserve category names and 2,1,3 heights.

exercises.prompt: Explain what explicit printing and figure-specification checks establish.
exercises.hint: Separate object construction, capture and browser behavior.
exercises.answer: Printing requests capture; data checks validate the specification. Actual browser rendering and interactions need separate observation.

reference:
d <- data.frame(x = 1:3, observed = c(2, 4, 3), rule = c(2, 4, 6))
p <- plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~x, y = ~observed, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", name = "Observed")
p <- plotly::add_lines(p, y = ~rule, name = "Rule: 2x")
p <- plotly::layout(p, xaxis = list(title = "Input"), yaxis = list(title = "Response"))
built <- plotly::plotly_build(p)
stopifnot(length(built$x$data) == 2, built$x$data[[1]]$type == "scatter")
stopifnot(max(abs(as.numeric(built$x$data[[1]]$y) - d$observed)) < 1e-12)
stopifnot(max(abs(as.numeric(built$x$data[[2]]$y) - d$rule)) < 1e-12)
unsorted <- data.frame(x = c(3, 1, 2), y = c(6, 2, 4)); ordered <- unsorted[order(unsorted$x), ]
stopifnot(identical(ordered$x, c(1, 2, 3)), identical(ordered$y, c(2, 4, 6)))
counts <- data.frame(category = c("A", "B", "C"), count = c(2, 1, 3))
bar <- plotly::plot_ly(counts, x = ~category, y = ~count, type = "bar", name = "Count")
bar <- plotly::layout(bar, yaxis = list(title = "Count", rangemode = "tozero"))
b <- plotly::plotly_build(bar)$x$data[[1]]
stopifnot(identical(as.character(b$x), counts$category), identical(as.numeric(b$y), counts$count))
print(p)
print(bar)
cat("r-057 reference checks passed\n")
solution_explanation:
The reference inspects resolved traces rather than only checking an object class. Observed data and a comparison rule have separate names, and the bar example preserves category identity with precomputed heights. A row-order control shows why line connections need an explicit sequence.

Exactly two Plotly figures are printed. The prepared worker can capture their JSON specifications offline; browser delivery, zoom, hover and accessibility remain separate visual/interaction checks.
